analysis.investment_thesis: Gravita is India's leading secondary lead/aluminium recycler sitting at the intersection of two structural themes — EV battery waste and EPR compliance mandates — with a 9-year net profit CAGR of 58% and a clean balance sheet. However, commodity-linked thin margins (~12% operating), volatile free cash flow, and a massive FY25 equity dilution (~₹1,100 Cr QIP inferred from equity jump ₹837→₹2,260 Cr) temper conviction at 31.7x trailing P/E.
key_strengths: Battery recycling structural tailwind: EV adoption creates exponentially growing lead/aluminium scrap supply; EPR regulations make Gravita's compliance services a near-mandatory B2B service.
Exceptional compounding track record: Revenue 27.6% CAGR, EBITDA 34% CAGR, Net Profit 58.4% CAGR over 9 years — execution is proven across cycles.
Conservative leverage with expanding returns: D/E of only 0.20, ROE/ROCE both ~21% — capital-efficient growth with headroom to lever up for acquisitions if needed.
key_risks: Commodity price dependence: Lead/aluminium scrap prices and LME metal prices directly compress or expand margins — operating margin has swung from 5% (2019) to 12% (2025), making earnings inherently volatile.

Massive FY25 equity dilution: Equity base nearly tripled (₹837→₹2,260 Cr), implying a large QIP; aggressive investing CF of -₹864 Cr signals capital deployment risk — returns on this capital unproven.
Inflated 'other income': ₹88/76/111 Cr in FY23/24/25 other income is 29-35% of reported net profit — core operating profitability is materially lower than headline PAT suggests.
red_flags: Other income comprising 35% of FY25 net profit (₹111 Cr vs ₹313 Cr PAT) warrants scrutiny — gains from subsidiary transactions or forex could be masking weaker core operations.
Free cash flow deeply erratic (-₹61 Cr in FY22, -₹56 Cr in FY24, +₹175 Cr in FY25) despite strong reported profits — working capital intensity of scrap procurement is a persistent concern.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Gravita is a genuinely interesting India circular-economy play but not yet a high-conviction Jhunjhunwala bet. The 9-year compounding is impressive — revenue grew from ₹430 Cr to ₹3,869 Cr and net profit from ₹5 Cr to ₹313 Cr — and the business sits on two real structural tailwinds: India's EV battery recycling need will grow exponentially as two-wheeler and four-wheeler EV adoption scales, and EPR regulations are forcing producers to use certified recyclers like Gravita. Promoter holding of 55.88% is stable, FII interest at 15.75% signals international validation, and D/E of 0.20 is clean. At forward P/E of 23x for a company growing 20-25%+, valuation is not unreasonable by my standards.

The reservations are real though. This is fundamentally a thin-margin metal processor (12% OPEX margin) with commodity price pass-through risk — unlike a consumer franchise, pricing power is limited. The FY25 financials show a dramatic equity raise (₹2,260 Cr equity vs ₹837 Cr prior year), which means per-share returns will need to be earned on a much larger capital base. The -₹864 Cr investing outflow in FY25 signals an aggressive acquisition/expansion phase whose returns are yet to be proven. And the ₹111 Cr other income boosting PAT to ₹313 Cr is a meaningful quality-of-earnings question. I would want to own this at sub-20x forward P/E with clarity on deployment of the QIP capital before taking a large position.
